Initial unsubmitted source-audited draft.

section1.p: Unsubmitted ProtoXEP draft, version 0.0.1. This document has not been accepted, assigned a number or approved by the XMPP Standards Foundation. It records the compatibility behavior in Monogram 0.2.195 at commit 4736f7eddb423192e5d68435879f0b0a88371168.

Normative words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY describe conformance to this document, not XSF approval. Existing deployed identifiers are retained; no urn:xmpp namespace is invented or reserved by this draft.

XEP-0382 hides a whole message or attachment. XEP-0394 supplies code-point spans but no deployed partial-spoiler child. This proposal documents the existing private child without redefining either base format.

A spoiler is an empty spoiler element in urn:monogram:spoiler:0 inside an XEP-0394 span. The inclusive start and exclusive end count Unicode code points in the original body, not UTF-16 units. Require 0 <= start < end <= body code-point count. A spoiler child MAY coexist with ordinary inline style children. It supplies no alternate text, URL, asset or action. Empty content and no application attributes are permitted on the spoiler child.
section1.example: The answer is 42
section1.p: Malformed bounds or unknown spoiler data do not authorize replacing body text. Clients MUST retain the readable original body. A fully hidden body MAY additionally use the standard XEP-0382 marker; that marker, not a private partial marker, carries whole-attachment hiding.

Supporting clients advertise urn:monogram:spoiler:0 in disco#info. Supporting clients initially obscure the range and offer an explicit reveal action. Unsupported clients can expose it. Previews intersecting a hidden URL SHOULD neither be fetched nor displayed, and notifications SHOULD redact hidden text. Revelation state is local UI state, not an access-control grant or remote acknowledgment.

Place ranges inside authenticated protected content when that transport supports extension encryption. The deployed legacy OMEMO compatibility path also accepts public spoiler positions as untrusted display hints applied only to decrypted body text. It MUST NOT treat those hints as authenticated or accept alternate text/links/styles through them. This exception leaks positions and permits an intermediary to change hiding; a strict confidential implementation SHOULD instead use text-only fallback on that transport.

example.caption: Extension child only; the span is defined by XEP-0394

section1.p: Clients MUST retain a readable textual representation, expose actions and state to assistive technology, and avoid making color, animation or an icon the sole indicator of meaning. Unsupported metadata MUST NOT hide the readable fallback.

Message text is Unicode. Fixed protocol tokens are case-sensitive and MUST NOT be translated; human-facing labels MAY be localized. Implementations MUST distinguish UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar/code-point offsets and UTF-16 code-unit limits wherever this document specifies them. They MUST reject invalid encoding rather than replacing bytes in an identifier or payment destination.

A spoiler is a presentation preference. The body remains available to unsupported clients, archives, accessibility tools and participants. Hiding MUST NOT be described as confidentiality or authorization. Reject out-of-range/code-unit-confused spans. Untrusted legacy hints may only obscure existing decrypted characters; they cannot create other content.

The conversation transport determines confidentiality. Plaintext, servers, archives and forwarded copies may expose the content. Application display controls do not encrypt data. Protect all sensitive content inside an authenticated end-to-end encrypted payload and do not derive private authority from unauthenticated outer extensions.
This document requests no IANA action. No media type or URI scheme is registered by publication of this draft.
This draft requests no new registration. Existing protocol namespaces retain their existing ownership and meaning.
Deployed identifier: urn:monogram:spoiler:0. This is a private compatibility identifier, not an XSF registration.

The following source files and implementation notes are pinned to the audited commit. Existing regression tests are implementation evidence, not an independent interoperability or security audit. Editorial review can change a future proposal, but changes to deployed wire syntax require an explicit version/migration path.
